```
$ python -m pytest tests/ -q
FF                                                                       [100%]
=================================== FAILURES ===================================
________________________ test_containment_always_merges ________________________
    def test_containment_always_merges():
>       assert merge([(1, 4), (2, 3)], join_touching=False) == [(1, 4)]
E       assert [(1, 3)] == [(1, 4)]
E         
E         At index 0 diff: (1, 3) != (1, 4)
E         Use -v to get more diff
tests/test_public.py:6: AssertionError
__________________________ test_point_inside_interval __________________________
    def test_point_inside_interval():
>       assert merge([(1, 3), (2, 2)], join_touching=False) == [(1, 3)]
E       assert [(1, 2)] == [(1, 3)]
E         
E         At index 0 diff: (1, 2) != (1, 3)
E         Use -v to get more diff
tests/test_public.py:10: AssertionError
=========================== short test summary info ============================
FAILED tests/test_public.py::test_containment_always_merges - assert [(1, 3)]...
FAILED tests/test_public.py::test_point_inside_interval - assert [(1, 2)] == ...
2 failed in <duration>
```

Fix the source so that the suite passes.

Constraints:
- Do not modify anything under `tests/`.
- Do not add new dependencies; the standard library is all that is available.
- Keep the public API of the `solution` package unchanged: `merge`.

summary: The visible suite now passes (2 passed). I changed only `solution/core.py`. The cause was in the merge loop: when a new interval was contained in the previous one, the code set the merged end to the new interval's end instead of the larger of the two, so `(1, 4)` followed by `(2, 3)` shrank to `(1, 3)`. The fix sets the end to `max(pb, b)`, and I restructured the loop so that exact duplicates are skipped first, then overlaps and containment are merged, and touching intervals are joined only when `join_touching=True`. Spot checks match the intended semantics: `[(1,4),(2,3)]` gives `[(1,4)]`, `[(1,2),(2,3)]` gives `[(1,2),(2,3)]` without the flag and `[(1,3)]` with it, and duplicate points collapse. The public `merge` signature and the `ValueError` on reversed intervals are unchanged, and nothing under `tests/` was touched.
